reject: Usefulness review — No practical use case is demonstrated. Describe a specific task and show who benefits from the plugin and when.
Usefulness review — The plugin does not simplify user actions or provide a meaningful result. Add a useful use case and demonstrate its benefit.
Usefulness review — Installation and setup are more complicated than the task itself. Simplify usage and show what work the plugin saves.
Usefulness review — The examples do not demonstrate the claimed benefit. Provide a before-and-after example showing a practical result.
Rule 2.5 — The author has not understood the generated code and cannot explain or maintain it. Review the implementation, fix defects and test all advertised features. Using AI itself is allowed.
Rule 2.5 — The generated interface has not been refined: arbitrary colors, excessive decoration, inconsistent elements or unreadable text. Make the design consistent and verify usability.
Rule 2.5 — The interface has not been adapted to the client and looks out of place. Use Telegram/exteraGram components or follow the same style, with clear actions and a tidy layout.
Rule 2.1 — Duplicate plugin: no clear advantage. Add new features or a measurable improvement over the existing plugin.
Rule 2.1 — The client already has this feature, including announced features. Add capabilities the built-in feature lacks.
Rule 2.2 — A single cosmetic edit or preset action. Turn it into a useful tool with broader capabilities.
Rule 2.4 — An inside joke with no practical value. Add a useful use case or explain why the meme is relevant to a wider audience.
Rule 2.3 — Crash on startup or during use. Fix the error and provide a working example on the current client version.
Rule 2.3 — Lag and excessive UI refreshes. Move heavy work off the UI thread and remove unnecessary refresh() calls.
Rule 2.3 — Broken UI or localization. Fix element placement and strings for the selected client language.
Rule 2.3 — Conflict with another plugin. Resolve the race or hook conflict and test both plugins together.
Rule 2.3 — Time-sensitive values are hardcoded. Refresh rates, links and other changing data or make them configurable.
Rule 2.5 — Generated code is unverified and contains errors. Review the code, fix the defects and test every advertised feature.
Rule 1.1 — Spam, artificial engagement or automated abuse. Remove bulk messaging, auto-farming, auto-invites and similar mechanisms.
Rule 1.2 — User harm or surveillance. Remove collection of others' data, phishing, hidden-online tracking and other harmful features.
Rule 1.3 — Hidden code download or execution. Remove the hidden mechanism; make permitted extensions and auto-updates explicit, opt-in and off by default.
Rule 1.3 — Unwanted actions without the user's knowledge. Remove automatic channel subscriptions and hidden data transfers.
Rule 1.4 — Fake verification or trust badges. Remove the imitation; only marking your own channel and yourself as its developer is allowed.
Rule 1.5 — Official resources are blocked or altered. Restore access and the original content of official project channels.
Section 3 — The fork's origin is undisclosed. Label it as a fork, credit the original author and describe the changes or fixes.
Section 3 — Cosmetic fork or fork of an actively maintained plugin. Add substantial changes and demonstrate eligibility under the fork rules.
Section 3 — Fork of a fork without both authors' consent. Provide permission from the original author and the author of the source fork.
Technical requirements — Invalid or unreadable metadata. Fix id, name, version, app_version and author; verify that the file parses.
Technical requirements — Invalid plugin file. Submit a valid file without encoding errors: .plugin without BOM up to 8 MB; .elyx/.eaf up to 100 MB.
Technical requirements — Purpose or instructions are unclear. Explain what the plugin does, where to enable its features and how to use them.
approve: Unique functionality, no equivalent in the catalog
Noticeably better than the existing alternative
Tested on the current version and working
Optimized, does not overload the client
Justified fork: the original is abandoned and no longer works
Rule 2.5 — AI-assisted code and interface have been refined and tested: the author understands the implementation, features work and the design fits the client
update_reject: Usefulness review — The changes provide no practical benefit over the published version. Demonstrate a useful new use case or a specific improvement.
Usefulness review — The update removes useful features without an equivalent replacement. Preserve those use cases or explain the change in behavior.
Rule 2.5 — The author has not understood the generated changes and cannot explain or maintain them. Review the new code and test the update alongside existing features. Using AI itself is allowed.

Rule 2.5 — The update introduces an unrefined generated interface: arbitrary colors, excessive decoration, inconsistent elements or unreadable text. Refine the design and test the usability of the new screens.
Rule 2.5 — New screens have not been adapted to the client and look out of place. Use Telegram/exteraGram components or follow the same style, keeping actions clear and the interface consistent.
Update requirements — The changelog is missing or unclear. List new features, fixes and differences from the published version.
Update requirements — No new examples of the changes. Attach separate screenshots or a video of the new version demonstrating the advertised changes.
Technical requirements — The update version is not higher than the published version. Increase version and submit a new file.
Technical requirements — Invalid minimum client version. Set a supported version and test the update on the current client.
Technical requirements — The ID differs from the published plugin. Restore its original id; submit a separate plugin as a new request.
Technical requirements — Update metadata cannot be parsed. Fix the required fields and verify that the new file parses.
Technical requirements — The update file is damaged or exceeds its size limit. Submit a valid file: .plugin without BOM up to 8 MB; .elyx/.eaf up to 100 MB.
Rule 2.3 — The advertised fix is missing from the file. Implement and test it, then describe the actual changes in the changelog.
Rule 2.3 — The update breaks a previously working feature. Fix the regression and test existing use cases alongside the new ones.
Rule 2.3 — The update causes a crash. Fix it and provide a working example of the new version on the current client.
Rule 2.3 — The new version lags or wastes resources. Remove excessive refresh() calls, costly hooks and unnecessary background work.
Rule 2.3 — The update breaks the UI or inline controls. Fix their layout and actions on supported screens.
Rule 2.3 — Update localization is broken. Translate the new strings and verify the selected client language.
Rule 2.3 — New hooks conflict with another plugin. Resolve the race or conflict and test both plugins together.
Rule 2.3 — Hooks, timers or UI changes remain after disabling. Release resources and restore the original state on unload.
Rule 2.5 — New generated code is unverified and contains errors. Review the changes, fix the defects and test the update.
Rule 1.3 — The update adds hidden code download or execution. Remove the mechanism; enable permitted extensions only through an explicit opt-in option, off by default.
Rule 1.3 — The update adds auto-subscriptions or hidden data transfers. Remove them and review every new network request.
Rules 1.1–1.2 — The update adds spam, artificial engagement, surveillance or user harm. Remove the prohibited features entirely.
Rules 1.4–1.5 — The update adds fake badges or alters official resources. Remove the false trust cues and restore official content.
Rule 2.1 — A new feature duplicates an existing solution without an advantage. Add a clear improvement or remove the duplicate from the update.
Section 3 — The update includes a fork without the required attribution. Identify the original, its author and your changes; obtain both authors' consent for a fork of a fork.
update_approve: Version increased correctly, update metadata is complete
Update tested on the current client version and working reliably
Reported bugs fixed, results match the changelog
Compatibility with the current exteraGram/AyuGram version restored
Useful features added without disrupting existing behavior
No critical bugs or regressions found after the update
Security issue or unwanted behavior fixed
Clean update code, no unnecessary dependencies or hidden actions
No issues with the update, the new version is ready for publication
Rule 2.5 — AI-assisted changes have been refined and tested: the author understands the new code, no regressions were found and the interface fits the client
